name: Delhi
summary: Split Delhi into Old Delhi's bazaars and mosque, New Delhi's avenues and tombs, and the Qutb complex in the south. Use the metro to avoid traffic and start early to avoid heat.
seasonNote: April to June is extremely hot; winter mornings can bring heavy smog and fog delays.
arrival: The Airport Express metro reaches New Delhi station in about 20 minutes; use prepaid taxis or ride-hailing apps.
gettingAround: The metro is clean, cheap and air-conditioned; use ride-hailing apps rather than street taxis.
cashTip: Carry small rupee notes for rickshaws, street food and tips; UPI is everywhere but is difficult for visitors.
foodTip: Try chaat, parathas, butter chicken, kebabs and kulfi; choose busy stalls and drink bottled water.
buyTip: Textiles, spices and handicrafts from fixed-price state emporiums or Dilli Haat.
baseArea: Connaught Place, or South Delhi near a metro station

connections.note: Gatimaan and Vande Bharat expresses from Hazrat Nizamuddin or New Delhi; book ahead.
Several express trains daily; about 5 hours by road.

items.name: Humayun's Tomb
items.summary: A red sandstone and marble garden tomb from 1570, the model for the Taj Mahal.
items.expect: Higher entry price for foreign visitors; calm, large gardens.
items.tip: Go in the late afternoon and add the Sunder Nursery gardens next door.
items.why: It is the first great Mughal garden tomb and Delhi's most beautiful monument.
flow: Enter through the west gate.
Walk the garden axis and climb to the tomb platform.

items.name: Red Fort
items.summary: The vast red sandstone palace-fort of the Mughal emperors.
items.expect: Closed on Mondays; security queues and a lot of walking.
items.tip: Buy the ticket online to skip the counter queue.
items.why: It was the seat of Mughal power for two centuries.
flow: Enter by the Lahori Gate and bazaar.
See the audience halls and marble pavilions.

items.name: Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk
items.summary: India's largest mosque, above the packed lanes and bazaars of Old Delhi.
items.expect: Intense crowds, noise and traffic; robes are lent to visitors at the mosque.
items.tip: Take a guided walk or a cycle rickshaw through the spice market.
items.why: It is the most vivid street life in the city.
flow: Visit the mosque outside prayer times.
Ride or walk through Chandni Chowk to the spice market.

items.name: Qutub Minar
items.summary: A 73-metre carved victory tower from 1193, surrounded by ruins and an iron pillar that does not rust.
items.expect: Busy at weekends.
items.tip: Come at opening for soft light on the carved stone.
items.why: It is the finest early Islamic monument in India.
flow: Circle the tower.
See the mosque ruins and iron pillar.

items.name: India Gate and Kartavya Path
items.summary: A war memorial arch at the end of the ceremonial avenue leading to the presidential palace.
items.expect: Crowds of families in the evening.
items.tip: Visit after dark when it is lit and the air is cooler.
items.why: It is the centrepiece of Lutyens' planned capital.
flow: Walk the lawns around the arch.
Look down the avenue to Rashtrapati Bhavan.

items.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
items.summary: A gold-domed Sikh temple with a sacred pool and a free community kitchen feeding thousands daily.
items.expect: Cover your head and remove shoes; scarves are provided.
items.tip: Sit down for the free langar meal, or volunteer in the kitchen.
items.why: It is the most welcoming religious site in Delhi.
flow: Leave shoes at the counter.
Walk around the pool and visit the kitchen.

items.name: Karim's
items.summary: A Mughlai restaurant in a lane beside the Jama Masjid, open since 1913.
items.expect: Basic rooms and brisk service.
items.tip: Go for an early lunch after visiting the mosque.
items.why: The family traces its recipes to the Mughal royal kitchens.
flow: Find the lane by Gate 1 of the mosque.
Order kebabs, mutton korma and roti.

items.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
items.summary: A narrow lane of shops frying stuffed parathas since the 1870s.
items.expect: Cramped benches and deep-fried food.
items.tip: Share two or three fillings between you.
items.why: A classic vegetarian Old Delhi breakfast.
flow: Pick a shop with seats.
Order potato, paneer and a sweet rabri paratha.

items.name: Bukhara
items.summary: A famous hotel restaurant for tandoor kebabs and slow-cooked black dal, eaten by hand.
items.expect: Very expensive by local standards; book well ahead.
items.tip: Order one kebab, the dal and a naan to share.
items.why: Its dal Bukhara is the benchmark version of the dish.
flow: Reserve in advance.
Share the sikandari raan or kebabs with dal Bukhara.

name: Jaipur
tagline: The Pink City of forts and palaces
summary: See Amber Fort first thing, then the palaces and bazaars of the walled Pink City. Two full days is enough, with sunset from Nahargarh Fort.
seasonNote: April to June is very hot; the monsoon runs July to September.
arrival: The airport is 30 minutes from the centre; trains from Delhi take 4 to 5 hours.
gettingAround: Use ride-hailing apps or hire a car and driver for the day; agree auto-rickshaw fares first.
cashTip: Carry small notes for rickshaws and bazaars; fort tickets can be paid by card.
foodTip: Try dal baati churma, pyaaz kachori, laal maas (spicy mutton) and a lassi in a clay cup.
buyTip: Block-printed textiles, blue pottery and gemstones only from reputable shops; ignore commission touts.

connections.note: About 4 hours by train or road.

items.name: Amber Fort
items.summary: A hilltop fort-palace of courtyards, mirrored halls and ramparts above a lake.
items.expect: Hot, with many steps; elephant rides are offered but discouraged on welfare grounds.
items.tip: Walk or take a jeep up at 8 am.
items.why: It is Rajasthan's most impressive fort.
flow: Climb to the main courtyard.
See the Sheesh Mahal mirror hall and upper palace.

items.name: City Palace
items.summary: The royal family's palace, with painted gateways, courtyards and a textile museum.
items.expect: A higher-priced ticket opens the private rooms.
items.tip: Don't miss the four painted season gates in the inner courtyard.
items.why: It is still home to Jaipur's royal family.
flow: Enter by the Virendra Pol gate.
See the peacock gate and the audience hall.

items.name: Hawa Mahal
items.summary: The 'Palace of Winds': a five-storey pink screen of 953 small windows.
items.expect: The famous view is from the street outside.
items.tip: Photograph it from a rooftop café opposite in the morning light.
items.why: It is the emblem of Jaipur.
flow: View the façade from across the road.
Go inside for the view through the windows.

items.name: Jantar Mantar
items.summary: An 18th-century observatory of giant stone instruments, including the world's largest sundial.
items.expect: Little shade, and hard to follow without explanation.
items.tip: Hire a guide or audio guide at the gate.
items.why: It is a World Heritage site that still tells accurate time.
flow: Start at the great sundial.
See the zodiac instruments.
items.best: Sunny midday, when shadows are clear

items.name: Nahargarh Fort
items.summary: A ridge-top fort overlooking the whole city.
items.expect: A winding road; taxis back can be scarce after dark.
items.tip: Arrange a return ride and stay for sunset.
items.why: It has the best sunset view of Jaipur.
flow: Drive up late in the afternoon.
Watch the city lights come on from the ramparts.

items.name: Johari and Bapu Bazaars
items.summary: Pink arcaded streets of jewellers, textile sellers and shoe shops.
items.expect: Bargaining is normal; many shops close on Sunday.
items.tip: Compare prices in several shops before buying.
items.why: The best place for block prints, bangles and embroidered shoes.
flow: Walk Johari Bazaar for jewellery.
Turn into Bapu Bazaar for textiles and juttis.

items.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB)
items.summary: A vegetarian restaurant and sweet shop in the old city since 1954.
items.expect: Busy and somewhat dated.
items.tip: Order the Rajasthani thali, then ghewar from the sweet counter.
items.why: A dependable place to try Rajasthani vegetarian dishes.
flow: Take a table in the dining room.
Order a thali and a sweet.

items.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
items.summary: A sweet shop famous for onion-stuffed kachori pastries.
items.expect: A crowded counter; eat standing.
items.tip: Go in the morning when they come out fresh.
items.why: Its pyaaz kachori is the city's signature snack.
flow: Pay at the till.
Collect hot kachori at the counter.

items.name: Lassiwala
items.summary: A hole-in-the-wall serving thick sweet lassi in clay cups since 1944.
items.expect: Several copycats next door; the original is shop 312. Sells out by afternoon.
items.tip: Go before noon.
items.why: A simple, famous Jaipur refreshment.
flow: Order a small or large.
Drink it on the pavement.

name: Agra
summary: Come for the Taj Mahal at dawn and stay for Agra Fort and the 'Baby Taj'. One night is enough; add Fatehpur Sikri if you have a second day.
seasonNote: Winter fog can hide the Taj in December and January; summer is very hot.
arrival: Fast trains from Delhi take under two hours; the expressway takes 3 to 4 hours.
gettingAround: Hire a car or auto-rickshaw for the day; battery carts cover the last stretch to the Taj.
cashTip: Buy monument tickets online; carry small notes for rickshaws and tips.
foodTip: Try petha (candied gourd), bedai with jalebi for breakfast and Mughlai curries.
buyTip: Marble inlay work from reputable workshops; decline unplanned 'factory' stops.
via: Usually by train or road from Delhi

connections.note: Gatimaan and Vande Bharat expresses; book ahead.
About 4 hours by train or road.

items.name: Taj Mahal
items.summary: The white marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal.
items.expect: Closed on Fridays; strict security and a long list of banned items.
items.tip: Queue at the east gate 30 minutes before sunrise with an online ticket.
items.why: It is the most beautiful building in the world to many who see it.
flow: Enter at sunrise.
Walk the garden axis, then go up onto the marble platform.

items.name: Agra Fort
items.summary: A red sandstone fortress of palaces and marble pavilions, where Shah Jahan was imprisoned.
items.expect: Large; a guide helps.
items.tip: Visit after the Taj and find the view of it across the river.
items.why: It is the best-preserved Mughal fort-palace.
flow: Enter by the Amar Singh Gate.
See the Jahangir Palace and the Musamman Burj.

items.name: Tomb of I'timād-ud-Daulah
items.summary: The 'Baby Taj': a small marble tomb covered in delicate stone inlay.
items.expect: Quiet, with few visitors.
items.tip: Combine it with Mehtab Bagh on the same side of the river.
items.why: Its inlay work is finer than the Taj's and you can see it up close.
flow: Walk the garden.
Look closely at the inlay and lattice screens.

items.name: Mehtab Bagh
items.summary: A riverside garden directly across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal.
items.expect: The riverbank itself is fenced off.
items.tip: Come for sunset to see the Taj change colour.
items.why: It gives the classic rear view of the Taj without the crowds.
flow: Arrive an hour before sunset.
Walk to the river end of the garden.

items.name: Fatehpur Sikri
items.summary: Akbar's abandoned red sandstone capital, with palaces and a great mosque gateway.
items.expect: Persistent touts at the mosque entrance.
items.tip: Hire a licensed guide at the ticket office only.
items.why: A complete 16th-century royal city, deserted after 14 years.
flow: Drive an hour west of Agra.
See the palace complex, then the Buland Darwaza gate.

items.name: Pinch of Spice
items.summary: A popular modern restaurant for North Indian and Mughlai dishes.
items.expect: Busy with visitors at dinner.
items.tip: Book or arrive early.
items.why: Reliable, well-made curries in a town of tourist buffets.
flow: Reserve for dinner.
Share butter chicken, dal makhani and naan.

items.name: Deviram Sweets
items.summary: A sweet shop known for Agra's breakfast of bedai puris with spicy potato curry and jalebi.
items.expect: A local crowd; counter service.
items.tip: Go for breakfast after the Taj sunrise.
items.why: The most typical Agra breakfast.
flow: Order at the counter.
Eat bedai, then jalebi.

items.name: Panchhi Petha
items.summary: The best-known maker of petha, Agra's translucent candied ash gourd.
items.expect: Many imitators use the name; look for the original branches.
items.tip: Buy a small mixed box; the saffron and paan flavours are popular.
items.why: Petha is the sweet Agra is known for across India.
flow: Taste a few varieties.
Buy a sealed box to take away.

name: Petra · Wadi Musa
tagline: A rose-red city carved into rock
summary: Stay in Wadi Musa and give Petra two days: the main trail to the Treasury and tombs on day one, the Monastery climb and high viewpoints on day two. Add a night in Wadi Rum's desert.
seasonNote: Summer is very hot in the canyon; winter can be cold, with occasional flash floods.
arrival: About 3 hours by road from Amman or 2 hours from Aqaba; JETT buses run daily.
gettingAround: Petra is explored on foot, around 15 km a day; taxis link hotels to the gate.
cashTip: The Jordan Pass covers the visa and Petra entry if bought before arrival; carry dinars for stalls inside.
foodTip: Try mansaf (lamb with dried yoghurt sauce), maqluba, mezze and sweet knafeh.
buyTip: Sand bottles, Bedouin silver and kohl; don't buy 'ancient' coins or fragments.
baseArea: Near the Petra visitor centre in Wadi Musa
via: Fly into Amman or Aqaba, then 2 to 3 hours by road
costNote: Petra entry is 50 to 60 JOD for one to three days unless covered by a Jordan Pass.

items.name: The Siq and the Treasury
items.summary: A 1.2 km slot canyon that opens onto the carved 40-metre façade of the Treasury.
items.expect: Crowds from 9 am; horse and cart drivers along the way.
items.tip: Enter at 6 am to have the Siq nearly to yourself.
items.why: The first glimpse of the Treasury through the canyon is one of travel's great moments.
flow: Walk the Siq from the visitor centre.
Stop at the Treasury, then continue down the Street of Façades.

items.name: The Monastery (Ad Deir)
items.summary: Petra's largest monument, reached by about 800 rock-cut steps.
items.expect: A steep 45 to 60 minute climb; donkeys share the path.
items.tip: Climb in the afternoon when the façade is in sun and the steps in shade.
items.why: It is bigger than the Treasury and far less crowded.
flow: Climb from the basin restaurant area.
Rest at the café opposite, then walk to the viewpoints.

items.name: Royal Tombs
items.summary: Four grand tomb façades carved side by side into a cliff of striped sandstone.
items.expect: Steps up to the terraces.
items.tip: Go inside the Urn Tomb for the coloured rock ceiling.
items.why: They show the natural colours of Petra's rock best.
flow: Climb the stairs to the Urn Tomb.
Walk along the terrace to the Palace Tomb.

items.name: High Place of Sacrifice trail
items.summary: A stair climb to a mountaintop altar, with a quieter trail down past hidden tombs.
items.expect: Strenuous and exposed; allow 3 hours for the loop.
items.tip: Go up near the theatre and come down through Wadi Farasa.
items.why: It is the best half-day hike inside Petra.
flow: Climb from the Street of Façades.
Descend via the Garden Tomb and Roman Soldier Tomb.

items.name: Petra by Night
items.summary: The Siq and Treasury lit by more than a thousand candles, with Bedouin music.
items.expect: Runs on set nights only, needs a separate ticket and gets crowded.
items.tip: Hang back to walk the candlelit Siq in quiet.
items.why: A different, atmospheric view of the Treasury.
flow: Start from the visitor centre at 8.30 pm.
Sit before the Treasury for the music.

items.name: Wadi Rum
items.summary: A protected desert of red sand and sandstone mountains, explored by jeep with a night in a Bedouin camp.
items.expect: Basic camps to luxury domes; cold nights in winter.
items.tip: Book a camp inside the protected area with a jeep tour and dinner included.
items.why: It is one of the world's most beautiful deserts, 1.5 hours from Petra.
flow: Drive to Wadi Rum village.
Jeep tour, sunset and a night under the stars.
items.best: March to May, September to November

items.name: Al-Wadi Restaurant
items.summary: A simple town-centre restaurant serving Jordanian home dishes.
items.expect: Plain surroundings.
items.tip: Try the mansaf or maqluba.
items.why: Good-value local food away from the hotel buffets.
flow: Take a table by the roundabout.
Order mansaf and mezze.

items.name: My Mom's Recipe
items.summary: A popular restaurant near the Petra gate for grills and Jordanian classics.
items.expect: Tourist-oriented but well liked.
items.tip: Convenient for dinner after a day in Petra.
items.why: Reliable food a short walk from the gate.
flow: Sit on the terrace.
Share mezze, then a mixed grill or lamb dish.

items.name: The Cave Bar
items.summary: A bar inside a 2,000-year-old Nabataean rock tomb by the visitor centre.
items.expect: Hotel prices.
items.tip: Stop for a drink right after leaving the site.
items.why: It is one of the oldest rooms you will ever have a drink in.
flow: Leave Petra by the main gate.
Take a table in the cave or the courtyard.

name: Luang Prabang
tagline: Temples and slow mornings on the Mekong
summary: A small peninsula of gilded temples and French-era villas between two rivers. Wake early, swim at Kuang Si, and do very little in the hot afternoon.
seasonNote: March and April bring smoke from field burning; rain falls May to October.
arrival: The airport is 15 minutes from town; the Laos-China railway links Vientiane in about 2 hours.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle the peninsula; shared tuk-tuks and minivans run to the waterfalls.
cashTip: Mostly cash in kip; ATMs have low limits, so bring some US dollars or Thai baht as backup.
foodTip: Try khao soi Luang Prabang, laap, sticky rice with jeow bong chilli paste and Mekong river weed.
buyTip: Handwoven textiles from Ock Pop Tok and crafts at the night market.
via: Usually via Bangkok, Hanoi or Vientiane

connections.note: Seasonal direct flights; otherwise via Bangkok.

items.name: Kuang Si Falls
items.summary: A tiered waterfall with turquoise pools for swimming, plus a bear rescue centre at the entrance.
items.expect: Crowded from late morning; water turns brown in the rainy season.
items.tip: Arrive at opening and walk up to the main fall before swimming.
items.why: It is the most beautiful waterfall in Laos.
flow: Shared van or tuk-tuk, about 45 minutes.
Walk past the bears to the top tier, then swim in the lower pools.

items.name: Wat Xieng Thong
items.summary: A 16th-century monastery with sweeping low roofs and a 'tree of life' glass mosaic.
items.expect: Cover shoulders and knees.
items.tip: Go late afternoon when the mosaics catch the sun.
items.why: It is the finest temple in Laos.
flow: See the main hall and its rear mosaic.
Visit the funeral carriage hall.

items.name: Mount Phousi
items.summary: A 100-metre hill in the middle of town with a golden stupa and a view of both rivers.
items.expect: About 300 steps; packed at sunset.
items.tip: Go at sunrise instead for the same view without the crowd.
items.why: The best overview of the town and Mekong.
flow: Climb from opposite the Royal Palace.
Come down the far side past the Buddha shrines.

items.name: Royal Palace Museum
items.summary: The last royal residence, with a glittering throne hall and the sacred Phra Bang Buddha.
items.expect: Closed at lunch; no photos, and modest dress required.
items.tip: Visit in the morning before the lunch closure.
items.why: It holds the Buddha image the town is named after.
flow: See the Phra Bang shrine.
Walk the throne hall and royal apartments.

items.name: Morning alms giving
items.summary: At dawn, lines of monks in saffron robes walk the streets to receive sticky rice.
items.expect: A religious ritual, not a show; some tourists behave badly.
items.tip: Watch quietly from across the road, without flash, and keep your distance.
items.why: It is a centuries-old daily tradition.
flow: Be on a side street by 5.30 am.
Watch in silence from a distance.

items.name: Pak Ou Caves by Mekong boat
items.summary: Two cliff caves filled with thousands of Buddha figures, reached by slow boat.
items.expect: The boat ride is the highlight; the caves are small.
items.tip: Take the morning boat and bring a torch for the upper cave.
items.why: A gentle two-hour journey up the Mekong.
flow: Boat from the town pier.
Visit the lower and upper caves.

items.name: Luang Prabang Night Market food alley
items.summary: The evening handicraft market and its food area of grills, noodles and coconut pancakes.
items.expect: Busy and smoky; choose food cooked to order.
items.tip: Try grilled Mekong fish and coconut pancakes.
items.why: The cheapest and liveliest dinner in town.
flow: Walk the craft stalls from 5 pm.
Eat in the food court area.

items.name: Tamarind
items.summary: A restaurant and cooking school introducing Lao food through tasting platters.
items.expect: Popular; book for dinner.
items.tip: Order the five-bites tasting platter and stuffed lemongrass.
items.why: The best explanation of Lao flavours for newcomers.
flow: Reserve a table.
Start with the dipping platter and sticky rice.

items.name: Le Banneton
items.summary: A French bakery-café known for croissants, opposite a temple.
items.expect: Pastries sell out by late morning.
items.tip: Go after watching the alms giving.
items.why: A reminder of the town's French past, and good coffee.
flow: Arrive early.
Order a croissant and Lao coffee.

name: Sydney
summary: Spend a day around the harbour, a day at the beaches and a day in the Blue Mountains. Ferries are transport and sightseeing at once.
seasonNote: Summer (December to February) is hot and busy; New Year's Eve is the price peak. Winter is mild.
arrival: The airport train reaches the centre in about 15 minutes.
gettingAround: Tap a contactless card on trains, ferries, light rail and buses; fares are capped daily.
cashTip: Cards are used for everything; tipping is optional.
foodTip: Try flat whites and brunch, fish and chips by the water, Sydney rock oysters and modern Asian cooking.
buyTip: Aboriginal art from ethical, artist-owned galleries; sun-care and surf brands.
baseArea: The Rocks, the CBD, Surry Hills or Bondi

items.name: Sydney Opera House
items.summary: The sail-roofed performing arts centre on the harbour, open for tours and shows.
items.expect: Free to walk around; tours and performances need tickets.
items.tip: Take the one-hour tour, or book any performance to see inside.
items.why: It is one of the 20th century's great buildings.
flow: Walk the forecourt and up the steps.
Join a guided tour or see a show.

items.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
items.summary: The steel arch 'Coathanger', which you can walk across for free or climb with a guide.
items.expect: BridgeClimb is expensive and takes about three hours.
items.tip: Walk the free footpath and climb the Pylon Lookout for a cheap high view.
items.why: The classic view of the Opera House is from the bridge.
flow: Take the Bridge Stairs from The Rocks.
Walk to the Pylon Lookout or across to Milsons Point.

items.name: Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
items.summary: A 6 km cliff path linking Bondi Beach with Tamarama, Bronte and Coogee.
items.expect: Exposed to sun and busy on weekend mornings.
items.tip: Start at the Bondi Icebergs pool and swim at Bronte on the way.
items.why: It is the best urban coastal walk in Australia.
flow: Bus to Bondi Beach.
Walk south, stopping to swim, and bus back from Coogee.

items.name: Manly ferry
items.summary: A 30-minute public ferry across the harbour to a beach suburb.
items.expect: Outdoor decks fill up on sunny days.
items.tip: Sit outside on the right-hand side leaving Circular Quay.
items.why: It is the cheapest harbour cruise in the city.
flow: Board at Circular Quay.
Walk Manly's Corso to the ocean beach.

items.name: Royal Botanic Garden and Mrs Macquarie's Chair
items.summary: Harbourside gardens with a point that frames the Opera House and bridge together.
items.expect: Free and open daily.
items.tip: Walk from the Opera House around Farm Cove to the Chair.
items.why: It has the best single view of both icons.
flow: Follow the sea wall from the Opera House.
Reach Mrs Macquarie's Point.

items.name: Blue Mountains
items.summary: Sandstone cliffs, eucalyptus valleys and the Three Sisters rock formation, two hours west by train.
items.expect: Cooler than the city; mist can hide the views.
items.tip: Take an early train to Katoomba and walk part of the cliff-top track.
items.why: A World Heritage wilderness within a day trip.
flow: Train to Katoomba.
Echo Point, then the cliff walk or Scenic World.

items.name: Sydney Fish Market
items.summary: A working fish market with counters selling oysters, sashimi and fish and chips.
items.expect: Very busy at weekend lunchtimes; the market has moved to a new building nearby.
items.tip: Go on a weekday and eat outside by the water.
items.why: The best place for Sydney rock oysters and fresh seafood.
flow: Walk the retailers.
Buy oysters and a seafood platter.

items.name: Bourke Street Bakery
items.summary: A tiny corner bakery famous for sausage rolls and ginger brûlée tarts.
items.expect: A queue out the door at weekends.
items.tip: Take away and eat in a nearby park.
items.why: A Sydney café institution.
flow: Queue at the counter.
Order a sausage roll and a tart.

items.name: Chinatown and Spice Alley
items.summary: Dixon Street's restaurants and a nearby lantern-lit laneway of Asian hawker stalls.
items.expect: Mostly card-only; busy on Friday nights.
items.tip: Friday has a night market on Dixon Street.
items.why: Sydney's Asian food is among the best outside Asia.
flow: Walk Dixon Street.
Eat at Spice Alley's hawker stalls.

name: Queenstown
tagline: Mountains, a lake and adventure sports
summary: A lakeside resort town ringed by peaks. Mix one adrenaline activity, one scenic day to Milford Sound or Glenorchy, and a slow day of wineries or walks.
seasonNote: Summer is for hiking and the lake; June to September is ski season. Weather changes fast year-round.
arrival: The airport is 15 minutes from town by bus or taxi.
gettingAround: The town is walkable; buses use a Bee Card, but a rental car helps for Glenorchy and Wanaka.
foodTip: Try a Fergburger, Central Otago pinot noir, lamb, and Bluff oysters in season.
buyTip: Merino wool clothing and pounamu (greenstone) from reputable carvers.
baseArea: Central Queenstown, or Frankton for value
costNote: Activities such as bungy, jet boats and Milford flights are the main cost and are not included.

items.name: Skyline Gondola and Bob's Peak
items.summary: A steep gondola to a viewing deck 450 metres above town, with a downhill luge track.
items.expect: Queues in peak season.
items.tip: Buy the gondola and luge combo; go up for sunset.
items.why: The definitive view of the lake and the Remarkables range.
flow: Ride the gondola.
Do a few luge runs and stay for the view.

items.name: Milford Sound
items.summary: A fiord of sheer rock walls and waterfalls, seen by boat cruise.
items.expect: A 12 to 13 hour day by coach; rain is common and makes the waterfalls better.
items.tip: Fly one way if the budget allows, or stay in Te Anau to halve the drive.
items.why: It is New Zealand's most famous natural sight.
flow: Coach via Te Anau and the Homer Tunnel.
Two-hour cruise to the Tasman Sea and back.
items.best: Any season; book for a clear day if flying

items.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
items.summary: The world's first commercial bungy jump, 43 metres above a turquoise river.
items.expect: Expensive; free to watch from the viewing deck.
items.tip: Watching is fun even if you don't jump; pair it with Gibbston wineries.
items.why: This is where commercial bungy began in 1988.
flow: Drive or take the bungy bus, 25 minutes.
Jump or watch from the deck.

items.name: Queenstown Hill Time Walk
items.summary: A steep forest walk to the 'Basket of Dreams' sculpture and a summit above the lake.
items.expect: A 500-metre climb; 2 to 3 hours return.
items.tip: Go early or for sunset, and bring a windproof layer.
items.why: The best free view in town.
flow: Start from Belfast Terrace.
Climb through the pines to the summit.

items.name: Glenorchy drive
items.summary: A 45-minute lakeside road to a tiny settlement surrounded by mountains.
items.expect: A winding road with few passing places.
items.tip: Stop at Bennetts Bluff lookout and walk the Glenorchy lagoon boardwalk.
items.why: One of the most scenic short drives in the country.
flow: Drive the lake road.
Walk the wharf and lagoon loop.

items.name: Arrowtown
items.summary: A gold-rush village of wooden shopfronts and a restored Chinese miners' settlement.
items.expect: Busy in autumn when the trees turn.
items.tip: Visit in April for autumn colour.
items.why: A charming contrast to Queenstown, 20 minutes away.
flow: Walk Buckingham Street.
See the Chinese settlement by the river.

items.name: Fergburger
items.summary: A burger bar with a worldwide reputation and a queue to match.
items.expect: Waits of 30 to 60 minutes at peak times.
items.tip: Phone your order ahead, or go mid-afternoon or late at night.
items.why: It is the most famous meal in Queenstown.
flow: Order by phone or queue.
Eat by the lake.

items.name: Amisfield
items.summary: A winery restaurant known for a long tasting menu of local and foraged produce.
items.expect: Expensive, and booked far ahead.
items.tip: Book lunch for the mountain view.
items.why: Among New Zealand's most acclaimed restaurants.
flow: Reserve well ahead.
Take the tasting menu with wine pairing.

items.name: Patagonia Chocolates
items.summary: A lakefront ice cream and chocolate café.
items.expect: A queue on warm evenings.
items.tip: Take a cone to the lakeside steps.
items.why: A simple pleasure with a big view.
flow: Choose flavours.
Eat by the water.
